title: Time crystals
provenance: WP0 worker-curated from general physics consensus; NO web access in Phase 4. Every claim needs a source check before WP4 uses this pack for scoring.

claims.claim: Physicist Frank Wilczek proposed time crystals in 2012 as systems whose lowest-energy state repeats in time.
Wilczek's original equilibrium version was later ruled out by a no-go theorem (Watanabe and Oshikawa, 2015).
Discrete time crystals are driven (Floquet) systems that respond at a multiple of the drive period, so they repeat more slowly than the push that drives them.
In 2016-2017 two labs (Monroe's trapped ytterbium ions at Maryland, Lukin's diamond nitrogen-vacancy spins at Harvard) reported observing discrete time crystals.
claims.source_hint: Zhang et al., Nature 543, 217 (2017); Choi et al., Nature 543, 221 (2017)

claims.claim: In 2021 (arXiv July 2021; Nature 601, 531, published 2022) Google reported an eigenstate-ordered discrete time crystal on a superconducting-qubit processor. The '20 qubits' figure was NOT confirmed by the abstract.

A time crystal is not a perpetual-motion machine or free-energy source: it needs a periodic drive and does no useful work. Do not say it 'takes energy from the drive' - in the many-body-localized versions it does not continuously absorb net energy (it avoids heating).

honesty_note: Never imply free energy or a perpetual-motion machine; the pattern is driven.
